questions.q: A workshop leader insists every character must learn something by the end. Who would most directly push back?
questions.explain: Ruhl argues the arc is one option that has become compulsory, often with a moral expectation.

questions.q: What does Ruhl mean by an Ovidian play?
choices: One with a secret and an obligatory scene
One that tells you the ending first
One that takes pleasure in sudden, complete transformation rather than gradual moral improvement
questions.explain: In Ovid, Daphne becomes a laurel; the change isn't earned through lessons.

questions.q: What does Ruhl suggest American dramaturgy often resembles more than Aristotle's Poetics?
questions.explain: A journey of moral improvement: what has she learned, how has she changed?

questions.q: How does Ruhl relate her Ovidian form to Paula Vogel's teaching?
choices: She offers it as an addition to the plot forms Vogel taught
She says it replaces all others
questions.explain: It's another option alongside the Aristotelian, circular, backward and repetitive forms.

questions.q: In Ruhl's adaptation of Orlando, the hero wakes up as a woman. How does that fit her argument?
choices: It's a total change the story simply accepts, without psychological justification
It's the payoff of a lesson learned

questions.q: Ruhl asks whether the arc's rising-climax-release shape reflects a cultural bias. How should a reader take this?
choices: As a rule for all plays
As a joke with no point
As a provocation and open question
questions.explain: Many of her essays end with questions rather than answers.

questions.q: What does Ruhl say about conflict in drama?
choices: Fighting can be dramatic, but it isn't the only way to make drama
questions.explain: She treats conflict, like the arc, as a tool rather than a law.

ideas: Characters don't have to learn and improve; they can simply transform, like Daphne into a tree.
The compulsory character arc owes more to The Pilgrim's Progress than to Aristotle.
A play can take pleasure in change itself rather than in moral improvement.
